WPT|/pf.lcc.why.title: Why the curves separate
WPT|/pf.lcc.why/0/0: The surface does not wear into the concrete
WPT|/pf.lcc.why/0/1: A bare slab dusts, pits and spalls under forklift wheels; every patch is a repair with downtime. The coating takes the wear, and a worn top seal is rolled on again overnight.
WPT|/pf.lcc.why/1/0: Cleaning is a wipe, not a treatment
WPT|/pf.lcc.why/1/1: Sealed pores do not drink oil, coolant or de-icing salt: the floor is cleaned with {R008} and water instead of being ground, stripped or replaced.
WPT|/pf.lcc.why/2/1: The elastic joint with {IPU} keeps water and dirt out of the slab joints; the edges, chamfered, do not break under the wheel.
WPT|/pf.lcc.why/3/1: What stays on the surface does not reach the reinforcement: chlorides and acids kept out of the concrete extend the life of the slab itself — the largest item of any life-cycle account.
WPT|/pf.lcc.note: Model, not a quotation. Nominal costs are summed as they fall due; present values discount every year’s cost at the rate set (ISO 15686-5). Downtime, slip accidents and the hygiene of the surface are not priced in — they favour the coated floor further. Replace the defaults by the rates of your project.

WPT|/rc.tech.label: Technology
WPT|/rc.tech.title: Crystalline waterproofing: how the concrete seals itself
WPT|/rc.tech.sub: What happens inside the concrete after {IC} has been brushed on: where the active ingredients travel, what they react with, why the seal is permanent — and what that means over the life of the structure. Schematic, at the scale of the capillary pores; not to scale.
WPT|/rc.tech.player: Micro scale · the reaction, step by step
WPT|/rc.tech.aria: 3D animation of the crystalline reaction in the capillary pores of the concrete
WPT|/rc.tech.hint: Drag to rotate · Shift + drag to pan
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/0/1: Hardened cement paste is porous: capillary pores of roughly 0.01 to 10 µm link up into a network, and micro-cracks join it. Under a head of water this network is the path — from the ground side through the wall into the basement, the pit or the tank. Capillary suction and pressure keep the water moving; it arrives on the inside as damp patches, salt bloom, drops.
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/1/0: The slurry on the matt-damp concrete
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/1/1: After the leaks are plugged with {F20} and the chased cracks and coves are made with {IM}, {IC} is brushed in two coats into the matt-damp, open-pored concrete. It is not a film that has to hold on the surface: it is a reservoir of active ingredients sitting on the mouths of the capillaries.
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/2/1: The active ingredients dissolve in the pore water. Driven by the concentration gradient — and by the moisture that a component under water load always carries — they diffuse along the capillaries into the concrete, even against the direction in which the water flows. The water that was the enemy becomes the transport medium: “foe becomes friend”.
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/3/0: The reaction in the pore walls
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/3/1: Deep in the pores they meet what every cement hydration leaves behind: calcium hydroxide (portlandite, Ca(OH)₂) and unhydrated cement grains. The reaction forms insoluble crystalline calcium silicate hydrate phases — needle-shaped crystals that grow from the pore walls into the pore space and interlock. The concrete itself supplies the second reactant: the crystals are part of the concrete, not a foreign material on it.
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/4/1: Where the crystals have grown, the pore is too narrow for liquid water: neither capillary suction nor the water pressure finds a passage. Water vapour still diffuses through the crystal network — the concrete stays vapour permeable (EN 1504-2 class I, sD < 5 m), so it dries out instead of trapping moisture behind a film. Impermeability to water: 14 bar (CRD-C 48-92); against negative pressing water: 1.5 bar.
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/5/1: Not all of the active ingredients are consumed. What remains lies dormant in the matrix for the life of the structure. When water reaches it again — through a new hairline crack (up to 0.4 mm), a settlement, a freeze–thaw fissure — the reaction restarts and fresh crystals close the new path. The self-healing that plain concrete manages only partly (autogenous healing) becomes reliable and repeatable.
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/6/0: Permanent: the seal is inside the concrete
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/6/1: The barrier is a crystalline structure inside the pore system, not a layer on the surface, so it does not depend on adhesion. The surface may be worn, abraded, tiled over or lose its brushed skin — the crystallised zone below remains and keeps sealing. It cannot peel, puncture, delaminate or age like a membrane, and it resists water pressure from either side.
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/7/0: Over the life of the structure
WPT|/rc.tech.steps/7/1: One application, no renewal cycle: the crystalline zone is as durable as the concrete around it and grows deeper for as long as moisture and unreacted active ingredient meet. Water that stays out is chloride and carbon dioxide that stay out — the reinforcement stays protected (carbonation reducing, chloride-free). The life-cycle comparison below turns this into figures.

WPT|/rc.tech.caps/2: The active ingredients diffuse into the pore water
WPT|/rc.tech.caps/3: Crystals grow from the pore walls
WPT|/rc.tech.caps/4: The capillaries are blocked — vapour still passes

WPT|/rc.tech.rxn.title: The reaction, in one line
WPT|/rc.tech.rxn.hyd: Cement hydration leaves free lime in every concrete:
WPT|/rc.tech.rxn.ic: The crystalline waterproofing turns that lime into crystals in the pores:
WPT|/rc.tech.rxn.icEq: active ingredients of {IC} + Ca(OH)₂ + H₂O → insoluble crystalline calcium silicate hydrate
WPT|/rc.tech.rxn.note: Simplified. The composition of the active ingredients is proprietary; the mechanism is that of crystalline waterproofing technology and shows in penetration tests, in micrographs of the needle-shaped crystals in the pores and in the standardised water permeability tests of the data sheets (EN 12390-8, CRD-C 48-92).
WPT|/rc.tech.needs.title: What the technology needs — and what it does not do
WPT|/rc.tech.needs/0/1: Concrete free of films, curing agents, laitance, paint and oil; the pores must be open, the surface saturated but matt — that is what the preparation with the high-pressure jet is for.
WPT|/rc.tech.needs/1/0: Moisture, to work and to keep working
WPT|/rc.tech.needs/1/1: The reaction runs in water: the coats are kept damp for 3 days, and later crystal growth needs water to arrive. In a dry component the active ingredients simply wait.
WPT|/rc.tech.needs/2/1: The crystals seal capillaries and hairline cracks. Voids, honeycombs, open cracks and running leaks are repaired first ({F20}, {IM}); the slurry is the last layer, not a filler.
WPT|/rc.tech.needs/3/0: Moving cracks and joints are injected
WPT|/rc.tech.needs/3/1: Cracks and joints that keep moving, or wider than 0.4 mm, are not self-healed: they are injected with {P1} / {P4} or filled with {IM} before the surface is waterproofed.
WPT|/rc.tech.needs/4/1: The crystals make the concrete watertight; they do not make it acid-proof. Where biogenic sulphuric acid or other aggressive media attack the concrete itself (above the water line of a sewage tank, for instance), a resistant coating protects the concrete — the crystalline seal below keeps the water where it belongs.
WPT|/rc.tech.cmp.title: Compared with the other waterproofing principles
WPT|/rc.tech.cmp.sub: The same questions put to four ways of keeping water out of a concrete component. The crystalline row carries the data-sheet values of {IC}; the other rows describe the principle.
